chapter: Forming the band in New York
title: Jimmy Mitchelle, Big Jack Marshall, Bob Range and Lee Stanfield
summary: Mitchelle became the band's singer, Marshall left, and Hawkins recalls childhood links to Range, Cap Sims and Lee Stanfield.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Well, Jimmy Mitchelle. Jimmy was, he was a sweetheart. You know, I didn't know he could sing until we got to New York. So, he told me, he said Hawk, let me sing that. That's how he started being a vocalist in the band. So, once he started to sing and it went over very nice, I liked it.
So, that's how he got started to sing. He was the third alto player in the section at that time.
The drummer, Big Jack Marshall, he got lost there. He went back, he went back to the hometown. And then, I added a couple other boys around there.
And, we got so many new, I'm trying to figure out what name I want to go to next that I can remember so much.

Bob Rance. He stayed in, we stayed kind of close together. I said that we went to Tuggle Institute together. And Cap, Sam, and I went to Tuggle Institute together. And, we also went to 'Bama State together. So, we were together all through those years. So, we knew each other as young kids.
A lot of the boys that I remember, Lee Stanfield, the bass player which was at Industrial High. His wife's grandmother was a teacher of mine in my kindergarten. That's how we happened to meet.
So, this grandmother used to switch me around in class cause I must have been a devil. Well, she had switched me maybe about twice. Taught me a lesson.
